title: Cohomology of a module sheaf agrees with that of its underlying abelian sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme with its small Zariski site [def-sc-zariski-site], and let $\mathcal F$ be any sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Write $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ab}}$ for the same sheaf after forgetting the module structure. For every $q\geq0$, the $q$-th right-derived global sections of $\mathcal F$ computed in sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-cohomology] and those of $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ab}}$ computed in abelian sheaves [def-sc-zariski-cohomology] are canonically isomorphic as abelian groups, naturally in $\mathcal F$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), first assertion, specialized to the small Zariski site of a scheme

proof.text: For the ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_X)$, the forgetful functor from sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules to abelian sheaves is exact, preserving kernels and cokernels, by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Thus an exact sequence of module sheaves remains exact after forgetting the module structure.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian: Mod(O) abelian and the forgetful functor exact)

proof.text: The sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ are the $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the underlying space of $X$, the objects of $X_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ being the open subsets and its coverings the open coverings [def-sc-zariski-site]; this category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]. Choose an injective resolution $\mathcal F\to I^\bullet$ in the category of $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves. Exactness of the forgetful functor from step 1 makes the underlying complex $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ab}}\to I^\bullet_{\mathrm{ab}}$ an exact resolution in abelian sheaves.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03DA and Injectives, Theorem Tag 079H, applied to the ringed Zariski site

proof.text: Each term $I^m$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module on the ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_X)$, so $H^q(U,I^m_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for $q>0$ and every open $U$, in particular $U=X$, by [lem-sc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic-zariski]; that is, $I^m_{\mathrm{ab}}$ is acyclic for $v=\Gamma(X,-):\textit{Ab}(X_{\mathrm{Zar}})\to\textit{Ab}$. The category $\textit{Ab}(X_{\mathrm{Zar}})$ is abelian with enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], so the acyclic-resolution criterion [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] (2) applies to $v$ and identifies the cohomology of the complex of global sections $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet_{\mathrm{ab}})$ with the derived global sections $R^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_{\mathrm{ab}})$ [def-sc-zariski-cohomology]. The same global-sections complex $\Gamma(X,I^\bullet)$ computes the module cohomology $R^q\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ [pqf-def-cohomology], since $I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution in $\mathcal O_X$-modules. The resulting isomorphisms are canonical and natural in $\mathcal F$, since maps of sheaves lift to maps of injective resolutions and the comparison map of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] (2) is induced by any morphism of complexes over the identity.
